coupling: The defect is spread over the two consecutive maintenance commits that rewrite the PFB private-dictionary segment loop in T1_Get_Private_Dict (src/type1/t1parse.c): 58d22ba9b 'Fix the segment merging' and 22a438daa 'Check the size'. Each commit's diff is, read on its own, correct and benign; the heap overflow only exists when both are applied. (1) Edited 58d22ba9b makes the incremental segment-merging loop tolerant of a truncated final PFB segment: after reserving the declared segment size with FT_QREALLOC(priv_dict, priv_len, priv_len + size), it reads with FT_STREAM_READ (which safely transfers only the bytes actually present) and advances the accounting by the DECLARED size (priv_len += size). Within this commit's own tree that is consistent: the buffer always covers priv_len, because the allocation grows by the same declared size. (2) Edited 22a438daa ('Check the size') hardens exactly that allocation: it clamps the QREALLOC to FT_MIN(size, stream->size - stream->pos), the bytes the stream can still deliver. Against the ORIGINAL 58d22ba9b code (which only advances priv_len after a complete read and bails out otherwise) that clamp is safe: a short read errors out before any accounting. Composed, the two edits disagree: for a final 0x8002 segment whose declared size exceeds the remaining file bytes, the allocation grows by the clamped 'avail' while priv_len (and hence parser->private_len) advances by the full declared 'size'. The loop then exits, parser->private_len exceeds the allocated block, and the eexec decryption (psaux t1_decrypt / PS_Conv_EexecDecode) plus all subsequent private-dict parsing read and write past the end of that heap buffer. A correct fix cannot be confined to one commit's diff: restoring the original reject-style size check in 22a438daa alone re-introduces the 'huge allocation on over-declared segment' behaviour that commit was fixing, and 'fixing' 58d22ba9b's accounting alone (advance by the bytes actually read) silently truncates the dictionary that 22a438daa's clamp was written to size correctly - only reasoning across both commits (clamp the allocation AND make the length accounting use the same clamped value) removes the overflow. Empirically verified: with only the 58d22ba9b edit applied the probe does not fire (no OOB; only the leak that the real unedited 58d22ba9b already exhibits on this input), with only the 22a438daa edit applied it does not fire (clean rejection), and on the composed tip AddressSanitizer aborts with a heap-buffer-overflow one byte past the clamped priv_dict allocation inside PS_Conv_EexecDecode, reached through FT_New_Memory_Face.
